clues: This small farming town lies in the east of South Africa. Green farms spread out all around it.
Rain falls here in every part of the year. There is no clear wet season and no clear dry season.
Dutch rulers may have first set up this town long ago. It took its new name in 1856 to honour a church man.
This town is a top place in its land for chicory crops. Its farms are also known for pineapples and for dairy cows.
By town lies one of the largest active dune fields in the world. A thin strip of wild forest, called Langebos, runs by the dunes.
